script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for December 4. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Paper with numbers.  Digital records in databases.  Why does money have value?

Money solves the 'double coincidence of wants'—needing someone who has what you want AND wants what you have. With money, you can sell to anyone, buy from anyone. This enables complex economies. Money stores value across time.  You work today, spend next year.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Money is a social agreement.  It works because everyone agrees it has value.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Money Reflection - What's Your Relationship?.

Here's your activity: What's your relationship with money—anxiety, comfort, scarcity, abundance? How does money affect your decisions? What would a healthier relationship with money look like? What can't money buy that matters to you? This helps you examine relationship with money.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how money works can be applied to money reflection - what's your relationship?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
